title: Parents, the French Opera, and attitudes to jazz at home
summary: His parents were old, his father died in 1913, and they lived in the opera world where non-operatic music was low. He recalls going to the French Opera with his mother and Mrs. Waterman.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: were quite old when I was born, and my father died in 1913 when I was just 10, and it had hardly emerged as an art farm. And it was just,

they grew up in the opera house, and anything that wasn't operatic music was flat crowd. The same could be true of my mother who lived considerably longer. Did you know anything about your parents' friends? Well, I was hardly at 10 years old, know any of the habits of my father's friends. And of course, your own great-grandmother was a good friend of my mother's, Mrs. Waterman, lived right behind us. And I remember going to the old French opera with Mrs. Waterman, my mother, as a little boy. So that's how I can say that I know my mother and Mrs. Waterman didn't go to any jazz parties. So that may answer your question. Well, when you were in high school and college, they tend to have ragtime or jazz bands at most of the parties you went to. They had those, what they called strip dances in those days. And a couple of people would get up a comedian and get up the dances, and everybody paid to get in. The couples would pay. And what they paid paid for the subscription act. I mean, what they paid paid for the band. There were a lot of... This is when you were in college? Well, that was current in college up to my day. I think from my day it began to die out. I'd heard them talk about my predecessors. But a lot of the guys, a lot of the bands about that time were like the 678 band, made up of college boys, or high school boys. I remember one very fine band was Dick Mackey. You've probably heard about Dick Mackey around here. In fact, I think Dick lived on the Gaul. His family lived on the Gulf Coast, where you were. And Dick Mackey had a band.
